title: Finite-cover presentations and cones of etale topos limits
statement:
Let $I$ be a small category and $D:I\to\operatorname{Sch}$ a diagram of schemes in the universe convention [def-weil-size-convention, def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. Write $E_i=\operatorname{Sh}((D_i)_{\mathrm{et}},\operatorname{Sets})$ for its small etale topoi [def-weil-pbc-etale-site, def-weil-pbc-topos]. A topos cone from a category $E$ consists of geometric-morphism data $q_i:E\to E_i$ [def-trf-geometric-morphism] and natural isomorphisms $q_{i*}(D(a))_*\simeq q_{j*}$ for $a:i\to j$, with the etale direct images $(D(a))_*$ [def-weil-pbc-direct-image], satisfying the composition cocycle with the canonical scheme-pullback pasting comparisons [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-composition]; their invertibility forces the unit equation. A factorization through a cone $p$ is a geometric morphism together with projection isomorphisms compatible with these comparisons. The predicate that $p$ is a topos limit means that every cone from a Grothendieck topos factors through it and every compatible family of direct-image natural transformations lifts uniquely. The presenting size bound permits testing on topoi equivalent to categories of sheaves with objects in $\mathcal V$ and values in $\operatorname{Sets}_{\mathcal V}$. A geometric-point cone is such a cone from sets with each inverse image naturally identified with the pointed-etale stalk at a specified morphism $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega_i\to D_i$ with $\Omega_i$ separably closed [def-pc-separably-closed]; algebraically closed geometric points [def-weil-geometric-point] give particular examples.

A finite-cover presentation of this system consists of a strict diagram $F:I^{\mathrm{op}}\to\operatorname{Cat}$ of small categories; evaluation equivalences onto the full categories of qcqs etale $D_i$-schemes, with coherent comparison isomorphisms to scheme pullback; precoverages whose members are precisely finite families evaluated to jointly surjective families; a colimit category on objects and arrows [def-weil-pbc-arrows-functor]; and the precoverage of images of stage covers, with the finite-cover site axioms [def-weil-pbc-finite-precoverage, lem-weil-pbc-colimit-of-sites]. It includes finite limits of the colimit category, terminality of the images of stage terminal objects, a cone of projection geometric morphisms from its sheaf category, and natural identifications of their direct images with restriction of sections to the evaluated stage objects, compatible with the pullback comparisons.

For $r:J\to I$, $D':J\to\operatorname{Sch}$ and a natural isomorphism $\epsilon:D'\simeq rD$, a comparison of two projection cones is an equivalence of their source categories and isomorphisms between its direct image followed by $p_{r(j)*}$ and $p'_{j*}\epsilon_{j*}$, satisfying the compatibility square for every arrow of $J$, using the naturality of $\epsilon$ and canonical pullback pasting. It is canonical when every other compatible comparison receives a unique invertible natural transformation from it respecting all projection isomorphisms. These are definitions of data and predicates, with no existence assertion.

reviewed_lean.note: Item theorem and new def node are mathematically right. Checked: every hypothesis (cofiltered I includes nonempty; qcqs stages and transitions); the stages and their equivalences to the qcqs etale categories, with the actual Over.pullbackComp cocycle; finite jointly surjective stage covers; the objects/arrows colimit site; the finite-limit and terminal clauses; projections normalized as restriction of sections; IsToposLimit (factorization of every cone plus unique lifting of all compatible 2-cells); separably closed geometric-point cones with pointSmallEtale stalks (per-stage form equivalent to the compatible-family form); invariance under any initial reindexing and diagram isomorphism, with a unique invertible comparison. Universes match etaleToposPoint_isGeometric and finitarySite_enoughPoints. Statements verbatim; docstrings with all 7 proof steps; only sorry is the theorem proof; no duplicate found. FIX (H12/H2): the new def node uses Cat.arrows (def-weil-pbc-arrows-functor), Etale.lowerStar (def-weil-pbc-direct-image) and Etale.lowerStarComp (recorded declaration of lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-composition) without citing them. fixes/def-per-qcqs-etale-limit-presentation.json adds the three stmt_deps and matching TeX citations; no Lean change, so no compile.
